about: The 12 rows where the 2026-11-06 judge and the blind Sonnet reading disagreed. Kevin sets 'expected' per row (CONFLICT, COMPLIANT, UNCLEAR or ADR-OVERTAKEN); labelled rows then move into job-search.json. Both readers' reasons are shown side by side so one row is a small decision, not a blank sheet.

cases.quote: The only rows that may leave the data are ones whose source row was removed.
cases.judge_reason: The new except branch keeps a failed row in results as 'not screened' rather than dropping it, which looks compliant, but the diff does not show whether a failed row is later listed or counted in the report, so this is left unsettled.
cases.blind_reason: A failed row becomes verdict not screened and stays in results and the report; nothing is removed.

cases.quote: A triage pile is listed, never hidden.
cases.judge_reason: The changed line only coerces a fact value to text when rendering the read/maybe piles; it does not hide, filter or drop any row or pile.
cases.blind_reason: The change only flattens a list value for display in fact(); it does not fold, hide or list any row.

cases.quote: A row the pipeline decides not to show is folded, not dropped: it stays in the data the report is built from
cases.judge_reason: The changed line only formats a field value inside the report and does not remove any row from the results.
cases.blind_reason: Display-only formatting of a field value; no row is dropped or folded by this line.

cases.quote: A module that needs a key imports it rather than hashing locally.
cases.judge_reason: The new recheck_cache builds its posting key with store.content_hash(r["text"]) instead of store.row_key; the text is already stripped, so the value may match, but the diff does not show that it is the same key.
cases.blind_reason: Uses the imported store function rather than hashing locally with hashlib; it is content_hash not row_key though.

cases.quote: Every table in `enrich/` is keyed on it and nothing else.
cases.judge_reason: The new rewrite_triage addresses the triage table by content_hash plus rubric rather than by row_key alone; the triage schema itself is not in the changed lines, so whether this breaks the obligation cannot be settled from the diff.
cases.blind_reason: The (content_hash, rubric) key already existed in the triage table at the parent; the new function just follows it.

cases.quote: The only rows that may leave the data are ones whose source row was removed.
cases.judge_reason: The new rewrite_triage path runs an UPDATE on the payload and deletes no triage rows, so no row leaves the data.
cases.blind_reason: The UPDATE rewrites a payload in place and removes no row; recheck leaves cards without source text untouched.

cases.quote: lands the rows in the shape job-feeds uses
cases.judge_reason: import_rows() is gone but cached_rows() still maps to the job-feeds row shape, so whether the 'import_rows() must land rows' obligation is met by the replacement is not settled by the diff.
cases.blind_reason: cached_rows() and _row() still emit job-feeds-shaped rows after the commit.

cases.quote: A failed fetch skips its row rather than failing the run.
cases.judge_reason: The try/except that skipped a row on failed fetch is deleted along with the fetch path, so the skip-on-failed-fetch behaviour no longer exists in the module.
cases.blind_reason: The try/except that skipped failed fetches went with the fetch path; no fetch remains in the module, so the rule is vacuous rather than broken.
cases.blind_notes: ADR ambiguous; cited line removed not added

cases.judge_reason: The drift report states that bin/li-descriptions.py does the fetching, which suggests another module invokes li-assist, but the diff does not show that file's code.
cases.blind_reason: bin/li-descriptions.py has called li-assist via subprocess since 2026-09-05; the commit only records that in a drift report.

cases.quote: No module builds a key by hand from a URL, a URN, a title or a raw description.
cases.judge_reason: The new `_role(company, title)` key is hand-built from a title and used as a lookup key, but it is a transient in-memory dedupe key rather than a stored posting key, so the diff does not settle whether the ADR covers it.
cases.blind_reason: Builds a lookup key by hand from company and title instead of using the row key.

cases.quote: A row the pipeline decides not to show is folded, not dropped: it stays in the data the report is built from
cases.judge_reason: The LinkedIn duplicate is never added to the row list: only its URL is appended to the twin's 'also' list and the loop continues, so the duplicate row leaves the data instead of staying in it as a folded row.
cases.blind_reason: The duplicate is not discarded; its URL is kept on the surviving row and printed in the report.

cases.quote: it is counted, and the count is visible in the report
cases.judge_reason: The report prints the folded copy's links as 'also on:', but the diff shows no count of folded duplicates anywhere in the report.
cases.blind_reason: Folded duplicates are shown as links but no count of them is reported, which the folded-rows rule asks for.
